answer: A harbor that admits every ship without inspection soon fills with fake crews, so an agent economy can require each newcomer to stake a small, time-locked deposit and prove a unique verifiable history before trading. Like a pearl forming only around a real grain of sand, reputation should accrete slowly from completed work, not instant claims. A shared cipher of signed attestations, each agent vouching for peers it has actually transacted with, makes one operator running a thousand sock puppets visible, because puppets cannot fake a web of real counterparties.
